_README: Every question the welcome interview asks, in one machine-readable file.
WHY THIS EXISTS: onboarding is a conversation, but a conversation isn't
repeatable. Fill this in once and you can rebuild the whole system from
scratch — stamp, hand the lead this file, done — then tear it down and do
it again identically. That makes onboarding testable instead of a
one-shot interview you hope went right.
HOW TO USE IT (three ways, all valid):
1. Ignore it. DM the lead and answer conversationally. This file is
never required.
2. Fill it in first, then tell the lead: 'my answers are in
<path>/onboarding-answers.json'. It reads, confirms the summary with
you, and persists — no interview.
3. Fill in part of it. The lead uses what's here and asks only about
what's missing or null.
NEVER PUT A SECRET IN THIS FILE. No API keys, tokens, passwords, or
webhook URLs — ever. Secrets live only in the OneCLI vault; this file is
config (repo names, channel names, ids, preferences). It is safe to commit
to a private repo, and scripts/check-onboarding-keys.sh fails if anything
in it looks like a credential.
'persists_to' tells you where each answer ends up. config.env keys are
read by bash gate scripts; project_config keys are prose the agent reads,
four of which setup-check.sh greps literally. Getting these two namespaces
backwards is the #1 cause of 'I answered that but nothing happened'.

decide_before_stamping._note: These two shape how tasks get created. Answering them late is expensive — see docs/INSTALL.md step 2.

timezone._ask: Your IANA timezone, e.g. America/New_York or Europe/Berlin. Asked before anything else because it decides when you hear from the system.
timezone._format: IANA zone name — NOT an offset like UTC-5, which cannot handle daylight saving.
_derives: config.env:OWNER_TZ (lead) — owner-tldr resolves your LOCAL hour at runtime, so the daily digest lands at 07:00 your time and follows daylight saving without anyone editing a cron.
Everything else is a cron line in task frontmatter and the kit pins TZ=UTC, so those DO need adjusting by hand before stamping.
timezone._action_if_not_utc: The daily digest needs no action — it uses OWNER_TZ at runtime. But the other 22 task schedules are UTC cron lines: edit the schedule: lines in your local copy BEFORE stamping if you want them on your working day.

agents_to_stamp._ask: Which agents do you want? 'support' (the lead) is required. 'local' is the recommended second: it runs on a local Ollama model, so it is always-on and costs nothing against the shared usage window, and it owns unanswered-watch — the task that keeps the community from hearing silence when the lead runs out of window. 'engineering' (the Reviewer) is optional. 'marketing' is optional and is NOT stamped by default.
agents_to_stamp._note: The value above is the recommended install: lead + local + Reviewer. Marketing is deliberately absent — it holds one task (content-draft-cycle) and can be added later without touching anything else. Stamping 'local' has a host prerequisite the others don't: Ollama running with operations.local_model already pulled (see PREREQS.md section 1). Without it the local agent stamps but cannot think.

primary_github_repo._ask: The project's main GitHub repo — everything else is inferred from this. Format owner/repo.

repo_map._ask: Per function: which repo, and a subpath if it isn't the repo root. Functions often SHARE one repo — docs and site are frequently subdirectories of product. Don't assume separate repos.
_derives: config.env:COMMUNITY_REPOS — space-separated list of repos to TRIAGE (issues/PRs/advisories/metrics). Normally every repo here, but it's the owner's call. Set on THREE agents: support (the lead), local, and engineering — each reads it for different tasks, so a repo missing from one is missing from that agent's work only.

config.env:MIRROR_REPOS — space-separated list of ALL repos above (including wiki, including ones sharing a repo) for repo-mirror-sync to keep checked out. Superset of COMMUNITY_REPOS; falls back to it if unset. LOCAL ONLY — repo-mirror-sync belongs to the local agent, so a mirror-only repo on any other agent's token is access nothing uses.

config.env:CONTENT_REPO — where content drafts get committed and PR'd. Needed by TWO agents, for different reasons and at different levels: marketing WRITES drafts there (content-draft-cycle) and local only READS pull requests there to find stale ones (draft-cleanup). Both hard-require it.
config.env:PRODUCT_REPO — the main repo, from repo_map.product. Set on the REVIEWER; docs-currency-watch watches its merged PRs.

config.env:DOCS_REPO — from repo_map.docs.repo. Set on the REVIEWER; where docs-currency-watch opens the docs PR. Leave it unset and that task stays silent forever: no docs target, nowhere to send a PR.
config.env:DOCS_PATH — from repo_map.docs.subpath, only when the docs are a subdirectory rather than their own repo. Lets the gate tell whether a merged PR already updated the docs itself.

wiki._note: A GitHub wiki is a real repo named owner/repo.wiki. Use null if the project has none.

triage_repos_override._ask: Optional: if you DON'T want every repo above triaged, list just the ones you do. Leave null to triage all of them.
triage_repos_override._note: Only changes COMMUNITY_REPOS. MIRROR_REPOS always covers the full map — mirroring is cheap and read-only.

docs_site_url._ask: Where you point people for how-to answers

topic_scope._ask: What's on-topic; anything else gets a friendly redirect

goals._ask: Which of the four jobs are goals for this project? Each yes makes a set of tasks eligible; each no keeps them paused. See welcome/SKILL.md step 3 for the task mapping.
goals._note: Every task below is labelled with the agent that OWNS it, because a 'no' has to pause tasks in the right group — the same goal now spans agents (awareness_growth, for example, pauses one marketing task and four local ones). The owning agent is derived from the task files; run `bash scripts/gen-task-table.sh` for the live mapping rather than trusting this list if the two ever disagree. FOUR tasks are deliberately in no goal list, because they are infrastructure rather than a goal: inbox-check (lead — and it stays paused anyway until an email MCP is connected), weekly-identity-integrity-check (lead), health-check (local), workspace-backup (local). Answering every goal 'no' does not stop those four.

community_support._note: Two things to know before answering. (1) unanswered-watch is the task the responsiveness goal actually rests on — saying no here pauses the one thing that prevents silence when the lead runs out of usage window, so pause it knowingly. (2) daily-github-triage and github-ops-triage cover the same ground; leave daily-github-triage paused when engineering is stamped, and activate it only as the lead's standalone-mode fallback.

audience_priority._ask: If growth is a goal: which audiences, in priority order?

github_bot_username._ask: The dedicated bot account's GitHub username — NEVER the owner's own. Every token is checked against this mechanically.
github_bot_username._note: Needs to land in BOTH namespaces: the scripts read the uppercase env key, setup-check.sh greps the lowercase prose key.

discord_display_name._ask: The Discord application's display name. Make it visibly match the GitHub bot username — this is the only agent with a public voice on both platforms, and a mismatched pair reads as two different bots.

channels._ask: Which Discord channels belong to which tier. Tier decides engage-mode, not per-message judgment.

support_auto_reply._note: Replies without being @mentioned. Needs --sender-scope all at wiring time.

announcements_channel._ask: If the team-lead tier has more than one channel, which is THE announcements channel? release-announcement-watch needs one unambiguous target.

discord_invite_url._ask: Invite URL to offer from GitHub replies when real-time chat would help, or null

maintainers._ask: Who counts as a maintainer for decisions the agent must not make

escalation_backstop._ask: The second human — name and contact — who takes abuse reports and urgent escalations when you're unreachable.
escalation_backstop._note: Going live without one is recorded as an open risk, not silently accepted. Code-of-conduct response is a human role everywhere it's done seriously — never an agent's.

target_audience._ask: Who is your content actually for, in your own words? e.g. 'church administrative staff and volunteer teams' — not 'developers' unless that's genuinely true.
target_audience._note: Marketing writes for this. Without it, drafts default to generic SaaS copy and the no-jargon rule has nothing to anchor to.

tone._ask: The register that follows from that audience, e.g. 'warm, practical, no engineering jargon'

docs_style._ask: Current-state only, or is version-history language ('added in 2.1') fine?

brand_source_repo._ask: Repo holding brand voice / content pillars / calendar, if different from the content repo

release_watch_repo._ask: Which repo's releases should trigger content drafting? Usually the product repo.
release_watch_repo._note: Unset means content-draft-cycle loses its release trigger and only fires on its weekly floor. If this differs from the content repo, the marketing token's repo-access list must include BOTH.

social._ask: Platforms this project has (for the follower series), which ones it posts to, and how each publishes.

profiles._format: list of public profile URLs — read-only, no credential

_mechanisms.intent-url: free, no key, DEFAULT — agent drafts, human clicks Post in a pre-filled composer
_mechanisms.paid-api: costs real money and is opt-in only; X has no free tier since Feb 2026 (~$0.20/link-post). Even enabled, the agent holds no posting credential — an OneCLI request-hold keeps a human button-press in the loop.

ga4_property_id._ask: GA4 numeric property id, or null for 'not now'

posthog_host._note: The script defaults to US. An EU project MUST set this or every call hits the wrong region.

onecli_dashboard_url._ask: What URL should the agent give you for the OneCLI vault dashboard — this machine, or a reachable remote address (e.g. a Tailscale IP) for checking in from elsewhere?
onecli_dashboard_url._note: 127.0.0.1 only resolves on the sandbox host. If you'll ever check from a phone or another laptop, give the reachable address instead.

workspace_backup_repo._ask: Private repo the workspace gets pushed to, or null to skip
workspace_backup_repo._note: This is the only thing that survives a sandbox recreate. The push is the LOCAL agent's job (workspace-backup), not the lead's — so this repo is the one place the local agent needs write access, and it needs it on this repo and nothing else.

github_actions_notifications._ask: Set up deterministic label→Discord notifications in CI? See examples/github-discord-notify.yml

gfi_label._ask: Your beginner-friendly issue label, if it isn't 'good first issue'

shared_inbox._ask: Shared project inbox address, or null. inbox-check stays paused until an email MCP is actually connected.

local_model._ask: Which Ollama model should the always-local ops agent run? Depends on host RAM — see docs/INSTALL.md, 'On a Mac mini specifically'.
local_model._note: On Apple Silicon the model shares unified memory with Docker and the sandbox, so total RAM decides: llama3.2 (~2 GB) for a 16 GB machine, gemma4:12b (~8 GB) from 24 GB up. There is no separate VRAM to fall back on. Only dev-metrics-report really stresses the model — test that one task's rule-following before spending RAM on a bigger model. This value must agree with operations.models.local; changing one without the other is a silent contradiction.

ack_grace_minutes._ask: How long may a community message go unanswered before the always-local agent posts a holding acknowledgment? (minutes)
ack_grace_minutes._note: A LOCAL-ONLY key — no other agent's config.env has it, because unanswered-watch is the only task that reads it. It is also the one value here genuinely worth deliberating over: too long and the silence you were preventing happens anyway; too short and the local agent talks over a lead that was seconds from replying, which reads as a broken bot to anyone watching. 20 minutes is a reasonable default. Must be a bare integer — the gate does arithmetic on it, and a value like '20 minutes' would kill it, so it falls back to 20 rather than dying on a typo.

models._ask: Confirm or override the per-agent model tier. Never Opus-class on a scheduled task.
models._note: Four agents, and one of them is not on a cloud tier at all. That split is the whole point of the arrangement: the three cloud agents share one usage window, the local one draws on none of it.

local._note: NOT a cloud tier. This is the local Ollama model and it must match operations.local_model above — same model, stated twice for two different readers, so change both or neither. Because this agent consumes no shared usage window, it can afford the every-10-minute cadence unanswered-watch needs, which no metered tier could.

first_response_grace_minutes._ask: How many minutes should a brand-new GitHub issue/PR sit before the lead replies? Default 15.
first_response_grace_minutes._note: Lead only, github-first-response (runs every 10 min). The grace exists so we don't beat a human maintainer who is already typing — replying 40 seconds after someone opens an issue reads as a bot rather than as attention. Lower it for speed, raise it if maintainers are usually first.

tldr_local_hour._ask: What hour (0-23) in YOUR LOCAL time do you want the one daily TLDR? Default 07:00 — the start of your day, so you are awake and can act on it.
tldr_local_hour._note: Resolved against OWNER_TZ at runtime, so it survives daylight saving. This hour also opens a 15-hour waking window: findings that mean we may be blind (a degraded fetch, a dead credential) escalate within ~4h DURING that window and otherwise wait for the morning digest, because escalating at 3am spends a wake to deliver something you read at 7am anyway. Genuinely urgent findings bypass all of this and arrive immediately, any hour.

docs_watch_max._ask: Max merged PRs to assess for docs impact per run (default 6). Only raise it if the project merges faster than that every 6 hours.
docs_watch_max._note: Reviewer only. The cap bounds cost — each PR costs one extra API call for its file list. Nothing is dropped: whatever doesn't fit surfaces next run, and the count is reported as `deferred` so a merge-queue burst is visible rather than looking like a quiet period.

docs_release_gating._ask: Hold docs PRs as drafts until the release that contains the change actually ships? Strongly recommended — say no only if your docs site is versioned separately from the product.
docs_release_gating._note: Not a config key — it is the shipped behaviour of docs-currency-watch, recorded here because it is a policy the owner should knowingly accept. Docs describing an unreleased fix are wrong for everyone reading the site today, so every docs PR is tagged with its version (the source PR's milestone) and held as a draft. release-announcement-watch surfaces the matching set when the version ships; a human merges them. A docs PR that misses its release is merged on approval or swept up by the next cycle — late is fine, early is not.
